scenarios.name: Complete fever interview — all stages

input.content: I have a fever and chills
If I understand correctly, the main complaint is Fever. Do you confirm?
How long have you had the fever?
Did it start suddenly or gradually?
Please inspect skin for rash or infection.
No rash visible, no skin lesions

output.currentHistoryTaking: The patient is a 45-year-old male presenting with fever that started gradually three days ago. He reports associated chills. He also reports a dry cough and mild headache.
output.associatedSymptoms: Patient reports dry cough and mild headache. Patient denies rash.
output.pastMedicalHistory: Patient denies any previous chronic illnesses.
output.investigations: CRP level is 78 mg/L. Malaria test is negative.
output.physicalExam: Skin inspection reveals no rash or skin lesions.
output.additionalNotes: Patient initially reported chills in addition to fever.

scenarios.name: Trauma — AVPU Voice, no investigations, wound exam

input.content: Patient hit his head on a crane
If I understand correctly, the main complaint is Trauma. Do you confirm?
Yes, laceration on the forehead, controlled with pressure
No investigations required for this case.
Is there visible deformity of the skull?
Is the laceration deep — subcutaneous tissue visible?
Yes, deep laceration, subcutaneous tissue visible

output.currentHistoryTaking: 33-year-old male patient hit his head on a crane. There was brief loss of consciousness lasting approximately 10 seconds. There is visible bleeding from a laceration on the forehead, which has been controlled with pressure. The patient reports mild neck pain.
output.investigations: No investigations required for this case.
output.physicalExam: Skull examination revealed no visible deformity. The forehead laceration is deep with subcutaneous tissue visible. Active bleeding is controlled with pressure, showing minimal oozing.
